candidates.evidence: Stated hint. Low confidence because the two strongest in-window FePS3 bands are off by 11 and 17 cm-1 from the 295-300 K bulk reference (Lee et al. Fig. 1b: P6 ~380, P5 ~280), no FePS3 reference band near 123 cm-1 is strong at 300 K, and the 74.6 and 550.7 cm-1 bands have no counterpart. Only one reference spectrum (arXiv:1608.04169) could be read, by eye.

hint_reasoning: Only one FePS3 room-temperature reference spectrum could be read (Lee et al., Nano Lett. 2016, arXiv:1608.04169, Fig. 1b at 300 K; Fig. 2a temperature series). Its 300 K modes are P1 ~98 (weak), P2 ~160 (weak), P3 ~230 (weak), P4 ~248 (weak to medium), P5 ~280 (medium), P6 ~380 (strong). The sample's strongest in-window bands are at 368.7 (FWHM 8.4) and 263.5 (FWHM 6.8) cm-1. The Si line at 520.9 cm-1 is only +0.2 cm-1 from 520.7, so calibration does not explain the 11 to 17 cm-1 offsets. The strongest FePS3 mode (P6, ~380) is therefore not matched, and the P5 comparison is also offset. A strong band at 123.6 cm-1 (FWHM 10.5) is not expected at 295 K: the 122 cm-1 Raman feature of FePS3 is a magnon below T_N ~118-120 K (McCreary et al., PRB 101, 064416, 2020, arXiv:1908.00608), and the 295 K reference shows no comparable band near 120. Extra bands at 74.6 and 550.7 cm-1 have no counterpart in the reference, and the 240.6 cm-1 weak band is 7 to 8 cm-1 from P4. The spectrum is therefore inconsistent with FePS3 at 295 K. The data alone do not identify the material: the library and matcher in the skill folder were outside the allowed directory and were not used.

limits: The skill's reference notes, the computational Raman database and its scripts live outside this folder, and the task restricts file access to the current folder. I therefore did not use the skill's matcher or the MPS3 reference note, and did not run rl_qc, rl_fit or match_library. The fit and checks were my own (scipy/lmfit, in this folder).

Literature mode positions were read by eye from Lee et al. Fig. 1b and Fig. 2a (about +/-3 cm-1). The full-text tables were not available: the iopic-bond ingest needs a VALENCY_BOND_TOKEN that is not set, and only one FePS3 paper was in the local library. Exact FePS3 room-temperature mode values from other sources are therefore unverified here.

The reference laser wavelength and polarization geometry for the Lee et al. spectra were not checked, so a small laser-dependent shift cannot be excluded. The 11-17 cm-1 offsets are much larger than the Si calibration (+0.2 cm-1), but they are not formally proven to be laser- or instrument-independent.

Fit uncertainties are noise-only (30 noise-injection refits): centre scatter 0.05-0.1 cm-1 for strong bands and 0.5-0.6 cm-1 for weak ones. Calibration adds roughly 0.2-0.3 cm-1. The lmfit covariance could not be estimated because of boundary/degenerate parameters, so these are not formal standard errors.

The noise is large (point-to-point scatter ~500 counts on a ~3500-count baseline). Weak bands near 150-220 and 650-1100 cm-1 are within noise and were not reported as peaks. The spectrum ends at 1099.75 cm-1, so bands above that cannot be assessed, and the 60-70 cm-1 low-wavenumber edge may suppress real modes.

The stated temperature (295 K) is above T_N (~118-120 K), so magnon features should be absent. A strong magnon-like band at 123.6 cm-1 at 295 K would be unexpected; it is most likely a phonon or an unidentified mode, but this is not resolved here.

Assignments for the 74.6, 123.6, 240.6, 550.7 cm-1 bands remain unknown: no reference counterpart was found in the sources accessed. The data alone do not identify the material, so the verdict rests on the mismatch with FePS3 rather than on a positive identification of another material.
